paper.title: Decomposition in Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steels
paper.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
paper.paper_scope: Experimental study of the different austenite decomposition reactions (discontinuous precipitation, precipitation transformation, cellular transformation, spinodal decomposition) in Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steels as a function of chemical composition (Al 9–12 wt%, Mn 10–30 wt%, C 0.4–1 wt%) and tempering temperature (600 °C and 800 °C for 30 min) after hot-rolling, characterized by optical/SEM microscopy, SEM-EDS and Vickers macro-hardness.

source.reason: Experimental procedure: 'Samples were heat treated at 600 °C and 800 °C for 30 min, followed by water quenching'; results and hardness tables refer to 800 °C tempered state.
Ingots of the 9Al-10Mn-0.4C grade were hot-rolled at 1150 °C and water quenched, giving the hot-rolled reference state.
9Al-10Mn-0.4C tempered at 600 °C underwent partial discontinuous precipitation (Fig. 1(a), Fig. 2(a)).
The 9Al-10Mn-0.4C alloy was also tested at 800 °C, where no austenite decomposition occurred (phase fraction diagram argument).
9Al-10Mn-1C hot-rolled reference state is reported with 273 HV in the hardening tables.
9Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C showed strong discontinuous precipitation and highest hardness (Table 2, Fig. 1(b), Fig. 2(b)).
9Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C developed cellular transformation plus spinodal decomposition (Fig. 5(a), Fig. 6, Table 5/6).
Ingots of the 12Al-10Mn-0.4C grade were hot-rolled at 1150 °C and water quenched, giving the hot-rolled reference state.
At 12% Al the reactions involved the whole γ volume; at 12Al-10Mn-0.4C precipitation produced a multifaceted microstructure (Fig. 3(a)).
12Al-10Mn-1C hot-rolled reference state is reported with 401 HV in the hardening tables.
12Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C underwent precipitation transformation (Fig. 3(b), Fig. 4, Table 4).
12Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C underwent full cellular transformation into γ + κ coarse lamellae (Fig. 5(b), Table 5).
12Al-20Mn-1C hot-rolled reference state is reported with 357 HV in the hardening table.
12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C showed full austenitic decomposition with cellular transformation plus spinodal decomposition (Fig. 5(c), Fig. 7, Table 5/7).
12Al-30Mn-1C hot-rolled reference state is reported with 324 HV in the hardening table.
12Al-30Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C had its austenite grains fully spinodally decomposed (Fig. 5(d), Fig. 8(e,f), Table 5).
9Al-20Mn-1C hot-rolled reference state is reported with 233 HV in Table 8.
9Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C showed hardening (359 HV) without detected austenite transformation, with κ + α precipitates along γ grain boundaries (Fig. 10(a), Fig. 11).
9Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C is reported in Table 8 (249 HV) and in the phase fraction comparison for 9Al-20/30Mn-1C.
9Al-30Mn-1C hot-rolled reference state is reported with 216 HV in Table 8.
9Al-30Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C showed hardening (330 HV) without detected austenite transformation, with κ-carbides along grain boundaries (Fig. 10(b)).
9Al-30Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C is reported in Table 8 (238 HV) and in the phase fraction comparison for 9Al-20/30Mn-1C.

unmapped_findings: Alloys were produced by casting in a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, yielding 0.5 kg ingots (b0026).

Characterization used optical microscopy, SEM (SEI and EDX/EDS) and Vickers macro-hardness with a 5 kg load and 5 indentations per sample; Minitab18 was used for data consistency checks (b0027, b0028, b0029).
The Fig. 3(a) caption labels the alloy '2Al-10Mn-0.4C' while the corresponding text refers to '12Al-10Mn-0.4C', suggesting a typographical inconsistency in the caption (b0023, b0035).
EDS measurements of local Al and Mn in δ, γ, κ and γ nano-κ phases for 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C, 9Al-10Mn-1C at 800 °C and 12Al-20Mn-1C at 800 °C are reported in Tables 3, 6 and 7 respectively.
Standard thermodynamic equilibrium for the Fe–Mn–Al–C grade is the 1150 °C hot-rolling temperature against which phase volume fraction diagrams were plotted (Fig. 9, Fig. 12).
